business_problem: UK Power Networks had real-time grid data spread across multiple on-premises servers and siloed teams, making access control, collaboration and timely business insight too difficult for cost-effective network operations and net-zero innovation.
solution_summary: UK Power Networks migrated critical datasets from a fragmented on-premises warehouse estate to the Databricks Data + AI Platform so real-time grid operations and predictive planning could run from a single environment. Smart meter alerts for power outages and voltage changes are provisioned in Databricks and shared across internal teams, while a Network Load Forecasting and Estimation machine-learning model uses the same platform for collaborative development between data engineers, analysts and data scientists. Unity Catalog simplifies fine-grained access management and promotes clearer data ownership as volumes grow, and Delta Sharing replaces ad hoc emailed extracts and one-off file shares with governed distribution across teams and external collaborators. By putting ingestion, analysis and model building in one workspace, UK Power Networks gains the visibility needed to understand constraints and faults quickly while supporting lower-cost network expansion and net-zero innovation.
